note: Three positions run without looking, then one set of frets heard from two roots: the old Variant selector set a key, so it is now two drones and two necks in one section, a minor pentatonic position 1 and, two frets lower, position 2 in the same frets. Moves holds any key and 80 to 100 bpm; both keys move together.

exercise.title: Three positions, two keys, no looking
exercise.why: Two minor pentatonic scales whose roots are two frets apart share three of their five notes, so in the same frets the shape changes only a little, and your hand has to know which root it is playing from.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. Play positions 1 to 3 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale and back, one note per beat, with your eyes off the screen. Then check the neck below for any note you were not sure of.
The goal of this practice is to cross from one position to the next without looking at the neck.
Press Play on the first drone below to start it. On the neck under it, play position 1 of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale from the low E string up and back down, and end on a ringed {{1}}.

Press Stop on the first drone. Then press Play on the second drone below: its root is two frets lower. The neck under it shows the same frets as position 2 of the minor pentatonic scale on that root, with the ringed {{1}} notes in new places. Play it and end on a ringed {{1}}.
When you change drones, your hand stays in the same frets and only the note you end on moves.
Practice until you can end a phrase on a ringed {{1}} over either drone.
